correctness.rationale: An endpoint removes one pair; an internal deletion of the middle of abc changes the profile by −e_ab−e_bc+e_ac. Enumerating the eight triples and four endpoint pairs gives six distinct changes. Translating by the original profile preserves distinctness. The pair-path formula imposes both endpoints, even when n=2 and they coincide (the sole pair disappears, giving N_1(2)=4). For a word with realized set S, summing t^|T|(1−t)^(6−|T|) over T containing S gives t^|S|, so the allowed-feature transfer enumerates exactly the desired statistic. Independently constructed all 64 matrices from the change vectors and computed their transfer fractions as bordered determinants: with U=I−zM_T, multiply det([[U,v_T],[−v_T^T,0]]) by z² and divide by det(U). After multiplication by J, each of the 64 fractions divided exactly as a polynomial; summing with binomial weights gives zero for each cross-product difference against the six frozen P_j/Q_j. This checks the identities for all lengths. A separate literal enumeration through n=14 also agreed. The first sixth-class term is 12z^9, with no lower term. Both cross-pair changes require opposite boundary pairs (probability 1/8 for n≥4); conditioned on them, disjoint triples entirely within the interior miss one of 000,111,010,101 with probability at most 4(7/8)^floor((n−4)/3). Thus the asymptotic limit is 1/8. The frozen scripts were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The projected deletion ball is a natural combinatorial observable: identical pair multiplicities can merge distinct edited words. Exact all-length class frequencies answer what is lost under this projection. The exact onset and nonzero limiting frequency of saturation give useful boundary data beyond the six-vector upper bound or a sample table.
